analysis: Integration of 16 units. The PR is a dependency-only change. desktop-app/package.json lines 32 and 39 move electron 44.5.1 to 44.9.1 and vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5, and desktop-app/package-lock.json follows (rolldown, oxc types and the binding packages move to 1.2.15 and 0.155). landing/package.json line 13 and landing/package-lock.json move next 16.2.6 to 16.4.1, sharp 0.34.5 to 0.35.5, libvips 1.2.4 to 1.3.4, nested postcss to 8.5.23, fast-uri to 3.1.9, undici to 7.30.1 and source-map-js to 1.2.2. The replayed patches show every changed entry resolving to registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity. They show no git, file or http sources and no removed integrity fields. sharp's hasInstallScript flag is dropped, which reduces install-time scripts. The manifest and lockfile versions are consistent (the landing next pin 16.4.1 matches the lock entry). New sharp wasm32 optional packages (freebsd, webcontainers) appear, but their lock entries were not fully visible. No provider, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest, key custody, prefix cache (T-041), fan helper or add-on socket code is touched. The threat-model boundaries TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 and TB-012 and assets A-001 to A-018 are unaffected. The desktop app and landing site are out of scope as console or marketing surfaces. Coverage limits: the patch excerpts were truncated, so I could not check the integrity hashes against the registry or inspect every new lock entry (landing head ~1599-1662, desktop rolldown bindings). Whether Electron 44.9.1 changes the packaging, signing or fuse configuration in electron-builder.ts was not visible. These are routine supply-chain hygiene questions, not demonstrated regressions.
